reopened_reason: the first direct T2-O component valuation law is falsified on every tested carrier

new_assertions.body: The exact T2-O scalar decoder is not a fixed per-component GF(2)^2 affine sum plus rank-phase offsets on any tested carrier.
The affine failure is not an unconstrained-fit artifact: the linear systems have only one or two active degrees of freedom after elimination and still contain contradiction rows.

Global rank-phase offsets do not absorb the remaining component-context dependence; if a linear component valuation exists, the scheduler grade must act on component values themselves or on higher-order interactions.
The scheduler-graded component monoid suggests the next minimal relaxation g(C)->g_r3(C), preserving XOR composition within a fixed phase while allowing the grade to change valuation coordinates.
Failure of phase-graded linear valuation would isolate the obstruction below global phase and force nonlinear decoder or interacting-component semantics within a fixed rank grade.
The exact bounded Q-V quotient (M2,r mod 3,T2) remains valid despite failure of a simple affine decoder; representation sufficiency and evaluator simplicity are distinct discovery problems.

the simplest stable independent-component XOR valuation is rejected in all eight tested T2-O carriers
